source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Lupin's Integrated Report 2024-25 states its API and CDMO businesses 'reflected strong alignment with global industry trends such as supply chain diversification, CDMO outsourcing, and high-potency APIs,' and that through API Plus and Lupin Manufacturing Solutions (LMS), Lupin is 'not only ensuring secure global supply chains, but also elevating India's stature in the global API and CDMO landscape,' citing India's CDMO market projected to grow from USD 3.5 Bn to USD 25 Bn over the next decade as global diversification away from China accelerates.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Lupin manages USD-INR, EUR-INR and ZAR-INR exposure through a mix of natural hedges and forex derivatives with layered hedging strategies overseen by group treasury.
inr_exposure.evidence: FY2024-25 Integrated Report financial capital/treasury disclosures describe exposure to USD-INR, EUR-INR and ZAR-INR fluctuations managed via natural hedges and forex derivative instruments.

pli_scheme.evidence: Industry commentary on India's PLI bulk-drug scheme names Lupin alongside Sun Pharma, Dr. Reddy's, Cipla and Aurobindo Pharma as having used PLI incentives to invest in domestic API/KSM manufacturing; not independently confirmed with a specific figure in Lupin's own AR text.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company selectively hedges a limited number of currency pairs where it has visibility and clarity, covering only a smaller subset of overall international business; hedging emerging-market currencies broadly is viewed as too costly to be economically justified.
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 management commentary: 'we do hedge a few currency pairs, which we have some visibility and some clarity on, but it's still a much smaller subset of currency and smaller percentage of overall international business.'

china_plus_one.evidence: Divi's Laboratories has publicly outlined 'unprecedented' capex plans -- including its new Kakinada greenfield facility (operational from January 2025) -- explicitly framed around capturing share of API demand shifting away from China under a 'China plus one' opportunity, targeting a share of roughly US$20 billion of APIs going off-patent through FY23-25, and is described as building niche API capacity in response to evolving China plus one demand.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports, largely invoiced in foreign currency and predominantly to Europe (~58%) and North America (~14%), made up ~88% of FY25 revenue, implying substantial USD/EUR exposure; no specific hedging policy percentage was found disclosed in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's Laboratories has a PLI-approved API manufacturing facility and is cited alongside peers (Aurobindo Pharma, Cipla) as having announced PLI-supported API/KSM capacity expansions; its new Kakinada facility is positioned to serve PLI/China+1-linked demand, though expected to become financially meaningful only from FY26-27 and no specific PLI-linked revenue percentage is disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: JB Pharma's international business rose to ~Rs 1,649 crore (~42% of consolidated revenue), with Russia and branded-generics exports recording double-digit growth via its Russian subsidiary (OOO Unique Pharmaceutical Laboratories); domestic business was ~58% of revenue. Company disclosures reference freight-cost escalation from geopolitical disruption and rouble-linked currency risk on the Russian subsidiary, but no explicit USD-exposure percentage or formal hedging policy was found in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: JB Chemicals does not appear on the published lists of companies approved under India's PLI Scheme for bulk drugs/APIs (Groups A, B, or C) found in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 segment mix (per investor presentation/results releases): India Formulations 21.8%, Consumer Wellness 9.6%, US Formulations 31.0%, International Markets Formulations 13.8%, Others (APIs/Alliances/Medtech) 16.1% of consolidated revenue. US Formulations is consistently the single largest segment. A clean domestic-vs-export geography split and hedging policy were not confirmed from primary AR text (AR PDF unreachable).

pli_scheme.evidence: Zydus Lifesciences (formerly Cadila Healthcare) is one of 9 domestic companies approved under Group A of India's PLI Scheme for bulk drugs/APIs, alongside Sun Pharma, Aurobindo, Dr. Reddy's, Lupin, Cipla, Glenmark, Intas Pharma, and Torrent Pharma.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party rating commentary (ICRA, April 2025) notes Natco has built a stable base of local vendors/suppliers for raw materials, KSMs, intermediates and APIs, reducing dependency on non-India sourcing to under 10% of total procurement spend. This is consistent with API supply-chain diversification away from China, though not explicitly framed as 'China+1' in the primary AR text (AR PDF unreachable).

pli_scheme.evidence: Natco Pharma is one of 9 domestic companies approved under Group B of India's PLI Scheme for bulk drugs/APIs (KSMs/Drug Intermediates/APIs), alongside Biocon, MSN Labs, Wockhardt, Alembic Pharma, Emcure Pharma, Macleods Pharma, Biological E, and Strides Pharma Science.

china_plus_one.evidence: Torrent commissioned API capacity at its Dahej facility for Penicillin-G (a fermentation-based KSM/API), targeting commercial production around mid-2024 under the government's PLI-driven push to reduce import dependence on China for key starting materials. Not explicitly framed as 'China+1' in primary AR text (AR PDF unreachable).

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue mix: India 55%, Brazil 10%, US 10%, Germany 10%, Other markets 15% (export total ~45%). No explicit hedging policy or USD-exposure percentage confirmed from primary AR text.

pli_scheme.evidence: Torrent Pharmaceuticals is one of 9 domestic companies approved under Group A of India's PLI Scheme for bulk drugs (fermentation-based KSMs/APIs including Penicillin-G), with API capacity commissioned at its Dahej facility.

rural.evidence: FY2025 city-tier sales mix (IQVIA MAT March 2025, cited in company investor materials): Metro 34%, Town Class 1 23%, Town Class 2-6 23%, Rural 19%.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 export revenue was Rs.2,061 Cr (14.4% of Rs.14,278 Cr total revenue from operations), up 34.5% YoY; no explicit USD-revenue percentage or hedging policy disclosure located.

pli_scheme.evidence: Public lists of qualified beneficiaries under the PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (e.g. Sun Pharma, Cipla, Dr Reddy's, Glenmark, Aurobindo, Lupin, Biocon, Torrent) do not include Mankind Pharma. Mankind sources some APIs (e.g. potassium clavulanate) from suppliers such as Kinvan that participate in the bulk-drug PLI scheme, but this is an upstream supplier linkage, not evidence that Mankind itself is a direct PLI beneficiary.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company/industry commentary indicates NAM-INDIA's earnings and debt-fund AUM/flows are sensitive to interest rate direction: earnings described as sensitive to "equity market cycles, interest rate trends and regulatory changes in India"; debt fund flows softened industry-wide (and for NAM-INDIA) amid rising yields, with expectations of inflows returning to fixed income as rates ease. Sourced from search snippets, not a directly confirmed FY2024-25 AR passage.

inr_exposure.evidence: NAM-INDIA operates overseas subsidiaries — Nippon Life India Asset Management (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. (MAS-registered, managing offshore funds/distribution across Asia, Middle East, UK, US, Latin America and Europe) and a Mauritius subsidiary. FY2024-25 AR (search-sourced): offshore business and GIFT City AUM of ~Rs.15,246 Cr; NAM Singapore offshore AUM ~USD 1.78bn as of March 31, 2025 (up from Rs.13,421 Cr as of March 31, 2024). No revenue % breakdown or FX hedging policy disclosure was located.

Third-party research/rating-agency summaries indicate IKS derives roughly 90-96% of revenue from US healthcare clients (India-based delivery, US-based revenue contracts), with remaining revenue attributed to Canada/Australia operations. Primary AR geography note and hedging policy text could not be directly accessed (source PDFs returned HTTP 403).

china_plus_one.evidence: Management commentary (Guruprasad Mudlapur, MD, Bosch Ltd) frames China as a competitive threat rather than a supply-chain-diversification tailwind: "China has developed substantial excess manufacturing capacity across various sectors, leading to intensified market pressures... there is a lot of competition coming in from that angle," requiring "strategic cost controls and strengthened supply chain safeguards." No text found attributing Bosch India revenue/order growth to supply chains shifting away from China toward India.

rural.evidence: Secondary-source commentary on FY25 indicates tractor and two-wheeler segments (rural-linked demand) were growth drivers: tractor sales grew on timely sowing, favorable monsoon, higher MSPs and improved farm liquidity; Powertrain Solutions division sales rose 5.8% driven by tractor segment growth. No explicit revenue percentage tied to rural markets was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Secondary-source summary of Bosch India disclosures: material cost increases attributed to product-mix shift toward traded goods and higher raw material prices, mainly steel and aluminum; company relies on third parties for raw materials/parts/components, and geopolitical events (Ukraine crisis) have impacted raw material price and logistics costs. No raw-material-as-%-of-revenue figure located; not crude-oil-specific.

inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary-source commentary notes rupee depreciation over the prior eighteen months "further complicated the business environment" for Bosch Ltd; Mobility business sector (which includes export-linked Powertrain Solutions) saw product sales up 7.0% in FY25 with domestic sales up 6.2%, implying exports grew faster than domestic, but no explicit USD-revenue percentage or hedging/forward-contract policy text was retrieved.

pli_scheme.evidence: Per public PLI-Auto scheme approval lists (Ministry of Heavy Industries / India Briefing / PIB), Bosch Limited secured PLI approval (~March 2022) under the Component Champion Incentive Scheme of the PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components — one of the approved Component Champion applicants alongside Bharat Forge, Ceat, Sundram Fasteners, Schaeffler India. Confirmed via third-party scheme-tracking sources, not a directly-read AR passage; no revenue percentage tied to PLI incentives was found.

rural.evidence: Company sells through a pan-India network of 60,000+ retail outlets with stated strategic emphasis on semi-urban and rural penetration alongside premiumization; IMFL (its core rural/semi-urban-skewed portfolio) contributes roughly 70-74% of total revenue from operations. No specific rural/semi-urban revenue percentage was disclosed in sources accessed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Analyst/press commentary on cost pressures notes: 'Glass bottles have increased about 20%, paper cartons nearly 100%, and logistics costs up roughly 10%. Surging crude oil prices and a weaker rupee are increasing import costs for packaging and other inputs.' No explicit percentage of raw material cost tied to crude-linked inputs (glass/PET/ENA) was disclosed in sources accessed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports account for roughly 9-10% of revenue (about 5-6% of volumes) per analyst summaries, implying limited but non-trivial foreign-currency revenue exposure; no explicit USD-denominated revenue percentage or hedging policy disclosure was located.

china_plus_one.evidence: Sell-side/analyst commentary (e.g. Moneycontrol: 'Navin Fluorine well placed for margin stability and China plus one tailwind') and third-party research describe Navin Fluorine benefiting from global specialty-chemical buyers diversifying supply chains away from China, with exports to key customers (Bayer Crop Science, Corteva, Fermion) rising as a share of exports, and long-term fluorspar supply contracts signed with non-Chinese (South African) miners to reduce China-controlled input dependence. No explicit 'China+1' framing was found directly quoted from the company's own AR/MD&A text in sources accessed (AR PDF was unreachable), so this is treated as analyst narrative rather than company-sourced.

crude_exposure.evidence: Third-party analysis notes fluctuations in fluorspar and other basic chemical input prices can impact profitability, and that China controls a large share of global fluorspar supply (a price-volatility/geopolitical risk factor); no crude-oil-specific percentage of raw material cost was disclosed in sources accessed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export share of revenue reported at 77% in Q4FY25 (23% domestic in that quarter), implying meaningful foreign-currency revenue exposure; no explicit full-year USD-denominated revenue percentage or hedging policy text was found in sources accessed.

pli_scheme.evidence: A Production Linked Incentive scheme exists for specialty/advanced chemicals and is discussed as relevant to the broader fluorochemicals sector; no source confirmed Navin Fluorine as a named/confirmed beneficiary or quantified any PLI-linked revenue.

govt_capex.evidence: Company/IR commentary attributes demand across its Mumbai micro-markets to infrastructure upgrades: 'demand drivers include infrastructure upgrades including the Coastal Road, multiple Metro lines, and the Mumbai Trans Harbour Link reducing commute friction across the city,' with the Mumbai Coastal Road cited as cutting Worli-Marine Drive travel time from ~35-40 minutes to 10-15 minutes.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Oberoi Realty carries a low-leverage balance sheet (debt-equity ratio ~0.16-0.21x recently; total borrowings ~Rs 2,816-3,300 crore; interest service coverage ~12x). Finance costs declined as NCD (non-convertible debenture, typically fixed-rate) balances were progressively reduced, suggesting fixed-rate instruments form a meaningful part of borrowings. Broader sector commentary notes real estate 'remains sensitive to interest rate changes, which directly affect home loan EMIs and buyer demand.' No explicit fixed-vs-floating percentage split was found in sources accessed.

Company-reported/analyst figures show average cost of debt declining through FY25 (from ~9.2% to roughly 7.68-8.65% across quarters, ending near 8.5-8.65% for FY25), alongside gross debt of roughly Rs 3,950-4,630 crore and net debt/EBITDA improving to ~0.9x. The steady decline in cost of debt tracking RBI rate moves implies meaningful floating-rate exposure in mall/construction financing, but no explicit fixed-vs-floating percentage split was found in sources accessed (AR PDF and IR site were unreachable).

china_plus_one.evidence: Company entered a China JV (60% stake, with Jinnaite Machinery) explicitly framed as building 'a geographically diversified, vertically integrated presence in the three key EV markets: North America, Europe, and Asia,' citing more secure access to local supply chains and 'reducing risk exposure.' This is diversification/expansion framing rather than an explicit China+1 (ex-China sourcing shift) narrative; no direct revenue/order growth was attributed to a China+1 dynamic in sources found.

govt_capex.evidence: FY25's largest acquisition was the railway business of Escorts Kubota Ltd, linked to Indian Railways procurement, described as supporting diversification across products/customers/geographies; no % of revenue tied to government capex was disclosed in sources found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Consolidated financial statements show a Cash Flow Hedge Reserve and Foreign Currency Translation Reserve, plus fair-value gain/loss-on-derivatives line items, indicating active use of forward contracts/derivatives to hedge FX exposure; exact policy text not directly retrieved.
inr_exposure.evidence: Company derives the majority of revenue internationally (~71% export in FY25 per regional breakdown: North America ~41%, India ~29%, rest of Asia ~6%). Historically ~74% of revenue was international in FY22 with 12-15% of raw materials imported (mainly from China), creating forex exposure partly mitigated by hedging (India Ratings commentary).

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first Indian auto component supplier to receive PLI certification (for its hub wheel drive motor for electric two-wheelers) under the Auto PLI scheme (total sector outlay ₹259 billion over 5 years); it filed seven applications for different products. Revenue/profit tied specifically to PLI-certified products was not separately disclosed in sources found.

rural.evidence: No consolidated company-wide rural/Tier-2+ revenue percentage was found. Partial signals: Nykaa's eB2B Superstore vertical reported 89% of sales from Tier 2+ cities in FY25, serving ~3.7 lakh retailers across 1,100+ cities; owned beauty retail store network expanded from 63 stores/34 cities (FY2020) to 237 stores/79 cities (FY2025); CEO commentary specifically cites Tier-2/3 cities (e.g. Faridabad, Ludhiana, Chandigarh) as driving higher average order values and expansion.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company set up an export-focused subsidiary structure ('Nysaa Cosmetics Trading' via Nessa International Holdings) targeting Qatar/international expansion; no revenue quantification or hedging policy disclosed in sources found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: IHCL has been net-debt-free at a consolidated level since FY22; as of Sep 30, 2024 the company had 'no significant debt except lease liabilities,' with unencumbered cash and liquid investments of over Rs 2,400 crore and undrawn credit lines of over Rs 300 crore at the consolidated level. No explicit floating-vs-fixed-rate debt percentage was found given minimal outstanding debt.

inr_exposure.evidence: IHCL's International Consolidated portfolio reported occupancy of 78% (+460bps) and RevPAR growth of 13%, with commentary citing ~20% growth in the US portfolio as a driver of consolidated results — confirming a meaningful multi-currency international revenue base (US, UK, and other overseas hotels/JVs) — but no explicit USD/foreign-currency revenue percentage or hedging policy text was found in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Only an unverified secondary-source paraphrase was located (not confirmed against the actual AR text): that Siemens Ltd (India) 'supplies certain products and components into the regional and global Siemens supply chain, leveraging its manufacturing capabilities and cost position in India.' No explicit China+1 framing or revenue/order attribution to China+1 dynamics was found in reliable sources.

govt_capex.evidence: Siemens India's Mobility (rail electrification/signaling, metro systems) and Grid/power transmission businesses are closely linked to government infrastructure capex; India is targeting infrastructure capex of ~10% of GDP. New orders booked in FY25 were ₹20,040 crore (+20.5% YoY vs ₹16,630 crore in FY24); order backlog stood at ₹42,250 crore at FY25-end (+6.2% YoY vs ₹39,770 crore in FY24). Siemens holds >50% market share in Indian rail signaling and is present in 11 of 20 Indian cities with metro systems (e.g. Kolkata Metro extension, Bengaluru Metro). No explicit % of total revenue tied specifically to government orders was disclosed in sources found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Only generic secondary-source risk commentary was found, noting that commodity price spikes — 'particularly copper and steel' — could squeeze margins if not passed through in contracts. No % of raw material cost or revenue tied to crude oil/commodity prices was disclosed by the company.
